hints: Notice the car moves distance $s$ along the slope of angle $\alpha$, so find the vertical height gained using $\sin\alpha$.
Recall gravitational potential energy gained is $mgh$ and work done by the constant force parallel to the slope is $F$ times $s$.
Write the ratio $mgh$ divided by $Fs$, substitute $h = s \sin\alpha$, and cancel $s$ to simplify.
walkthrough: Work done by a force parallel to displacement is force times distance, so work done by $F$ is $W = Fs$.
Gravitational potential energy gained depends on vertical height $h$, with $\Delta E_p = mgh$.
From the slope triangle, the vertical height for distance $s$ along a slope at angle $\alpha$ is $h = s \sin\alpha$.
Form the ratio $\frac{\Delta E_p}{W} = \frac{mgs \sin\alpha}{Fs}$ and cancel $s$ to give $\frac{mg \sin\alpha}{F}$. This is option D.

options.A: Divides by $Fv$, which is power not work, so $\frac{mgs \sin\alpha}{Fv}$ has units of time and cannot be the required energy ratio.
options.B: Gives $\frac{mv}{Fs}$, which is not an energy over an energy and ignores the vertical height $s \sin\alpha$ that determines gravitational potential energy.
options.C: Gives $\frac{mv^2}{2Fs}$, which is kinetic energy divided by work, but velocity $v$ is constant so no net kinetic energy is gained.
options.D: Equals $\frac{mgs \sin\alpha}{Fs} = \frac{mg \sin\alpha}{F}$, the ratio of $mgh$ gained to work $Fs$ done.
